A woman identified only as Edith "N" was detained in downtown Tampico on Oct. 26 in connection with the deaths of eight people in Nuevo Laredo in September 2019, according to the Tamaulipas Attorney General's Office, as reported Oct. 28.

The arrest was carried out under an order issued by a control judge, the state prosecutor's office said. Edith "N" faces alleged probable responsibility for aggravated homicide, abuse of authority, false statements to an authority and trespassing, according to the report.

The prosecutor's office did not specify what role Edith "N" allegedly played in the 2019 events, which left eight people dead in Nuevo Laredo. After her capture, she was placed at the disposal of the competent authority to continue the legal process. Her responsibility must be determined through the judicial process, under the presumption of innocence.

The case is one of the most serious unresolved episodes tied to Nuevo Laredo's recent history, and the arrest marks a new step in an investigation that stretches back more than seven years. The state prosecutor's office said it will follow the case in line with legality and due process.

Update — November 10, 2026

A control judge has ordered Edith "N" bound over for trial — vinculación a proceso — for her alleged role in the September 2019 deaths of eight people in Nuevo Laredo, the Tamaulipas state prosecutor's office announced November 10. After hearing arguments from both sides, the judge found probable cause on charges of aggravated homicide, abuse of authority, false statements to an authority, and unlawful entry into a home, and set a six-month period for the complementary investigation. Edith "N" was detained in Tampico in late October. She remains presumed innocent unless proven guilty through the judicial process.

Sources:

  • Fiscalía General de Justicia del Estado de Tamaulipas, via Blog Informativo, "Detienen en Tampico a Edith 'N' por caso de ocho personas asesinadas en Nuevo Laredo," Oct. 28, 2026
